ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Using the diagram, three 1-liter flasks are connected to a 3-liter flask by valves. The 3-liter flask has the relative number of helium atoms indicated. Initially, the entire system is at 585 K. The first flask contains oxygen, the second contains hydrogen, and the third contains nitrogen. The pressure of hydrogen is 3.00 atm, and the number of gas molecules is proportional to their representations in the flasks. If all the valves are opened, what will be the pressure in the system? Assume the connections have negligible volume.

The upper-left flask is labeled O2 and has 5 O2 molecular units drawn; the upper-right flask is labeled H2 and has 6 H2 molecular units drawn; the lower flask is labeled N2 and has 7 N2 molecular units drawn; the middle 3 L flask has 6 He atomic units drawn. Reasoning: The problem states that the number of gas molecules is proportional to the quantities shown in the figure, and the pressure of the 1 L flask containing H2 is 3.00 atm. Because H2 has 6 illustrated units, the nRT corresponding to each illustrated unit is (3.00 atm)(1 L)/6 = 0.50 atm·L. The total number of illustrated units of all gases is 5 + 6 + 7 + 6 = 24, so total nRT = 24 × 0.50 = 12 atm·L. After all valves are opened, the total volume is 1 L + 1 L + 1 L + 3 L = 6 L. The final pressure P = (total nRT)/(total volume) = 12 atm·L / 6 L = 2.0 atm.

method.method_draft: Count all drawn gas units from the image: 5 O2 + 6 H2 + 7 N2 + 6 He = 24 total proportional units. From the text, the H2 flask is 1 L and has pressure 3.00 atm; the image shows 6 H2 units, so each drawn unit corresponds to (3.00 atm)(1 L)/6 = 0.50 atm·L of nRT. The total nRT for all gases is 24 × 0.50 = 12 atm·L. When all valves open, the total volume is 1 + 1 + 1 + 3 = 6 L. Therefore P_final = 12 atm·L / 6 L = 2.0 atm.
